To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
people thrive to the degree that they feel competent, autonomous, and related.
people are more likely to live happily ever after when their innate psychological needs are satisfied.
the satisfaction of basic psychological needs for competence, autonomy, relatedness, and physical well being are necessary for psychological growth and well being.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extent to which the social ecological conditions in which people live and grow facilitate versus forestall self determined behavior and well being.
human beings as proactive beings whose tendencies toward well being and growth can be facilitated or undermined by the social contexts in which they live and grow.
the conditions that promote versus undermine self determined behavior and psychological growth and development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
human beings have a natural propensity toward growth and well being.

self determination theory has been successful in its efforts to explain the nature and nurture of intrinsic motivation and related aspects of healthy human functioning, including the processes by which the satisfaction of psychological needs contributes to these outcomes.
self determination theory is a general theory of human motivation, development, and health that has been supported by a broad and diverse range of empirical findings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
self determination theory has provided a conceptual framework that can help explain how people come to be who they are and why they do what they do.
the satisfaction of innate psychological needs is a prerequisite for optimal motivation, personal development, and well functioning.

human beings have a natural tendency to develop a sense of self as a causal agent, to be autonomous, and to interact meaningfully with others, and that these tendencies are enhanced by supportive social contexts and undermined by controlling ones.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the social context can be arranged in ways that facilitate or thwart the satisfaction of innate psychological needs, thereby promoting or impeding self motivation, social development and psychological well being.
human behavior is not determined by the environment, but rather is regulated by psychological processes.

people have an inherent tendency to be active, to seek out challenges, to expand their repertoire of skills, to explore their options, and to exercise a degree of choice and self regulation in their lives.
